title: Locus-Coeruleus Norepinephrine functioning as a predictor of childhood mental health
summary:
What is the research question?

Mental illnesses have become one of the main causes of health limitations. Currently, we mostly treat mental illnesses only after people have suffered from them for a long time. We know that a person's mental suffering often begins in childhood. An anxiety disorder as a child increases the risk of a (more difficult to treat) depression as an adult. The central question of LOCUS-MENTAL is whether we can predict the risk of mental illnesses. Children with an increased risk could then be specifically supported to prevent an initial illness.

How is it practically implemented?

We focus on the observation that people are differently susceptible to stress. Some children thrive even under adverse circumstances, while others are overwhelmed by everyday challenges. A modulatory system in the brain, the Locus Coeruleus – Norepinephrine System (LC-NE), likely plays a significant role in this. The LC-NE describes a very small area on the brainstem responsible for the neurosynthesis of norepinephrine and distributes it with its connections in the brain.

Animal models and initial studies in humans have shown that the activity of the LC-NE predicts whether people respond to challenging situations with mental distress. We imagine this system as a translator that helps determine whether we experience stressful situations as stressful. My previous studies have shown that we can measure this system well. To do this, we unobtrusively observe the eyes of children with cameras and record the changes in the pupil with high temporal and spatial resolution. This technique allows us to measure even heavily burdened or very young children without much strain.

Specifically, a longitudinal study is to be conducted in the research proposal, in which we measure the changes in the pupil in as many preschool children as possible. Then we look at how well the pupil response predicts mental stress in elementary school age. Additionally, we record other biological parameters such as cortisol in saliva and hair samples and determine the temperament of the children using questionnaires to connect this with the LC-NE system.

Why is this medically relevant?

In medicine, the experience of stress is often reduced to endocrine reactions, whereas psychology strongly focuses on the subjective experience of stressful situations. Our approach aims to combine these two perspectives.

Why is this interesting to the public?

The toddlers are to be recorded in the outpatient clinic of our hospital. This allows us to depict a broad spectrum of children who are at increased risk of mental suffering. With LOCUS-MENTAL, our outpatient clinic is to be expanded into an "early detection consultation." This way, we can hopefully identify and specifically support at-risk children earlier, so that mental illnesses can be better prevented in the future.

interventions.name: LOCUS-MENTAL will achieve its objectives by combining pupillometric indices of LC-NE functioning with a prospective panel design. Pupillometry is assessed by video-based eye tracking during basic paradigms that are feasible in preschoolers. Transdiagnostic psychopathology is assessed by questionnair
